text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn and his Dutch host Prime Minister Wim Kok announced that they will establish a joint fund to support small and medium-size companies in Hungary. @

- President Arpad Goncz, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy, and National Bank President Gyorgy Suranyi will be in Davos, Switzerland today to represent Hungary at the annual six-day meeting of the world's senior business figures and politicians, the World Economic Forum.
- The Socialist parliamentary group decided to throw its weight behind the government's three-tiered pension concept.
- Brau-Union AG announced on Thursday that it will merge the Martfu brewery into the Soproni brewery. Trading in both Martfu and Sopron shares was suspended at the stock exchange yesterday. @
- Inter-Europa Bank is planning to raise its HUF 2.807 billion registered capital twice this year, said managing director Pier Franco Rubatto.

-The US State Department's human rights report says that social discrimination against Gypsies and their disadvantageous state in virtually all walks of life continue to represent a serious problem in Hungary.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- All parliamentary parties agreed with the prime minister's proposal that the next parliamentary elections be held in May, 1998. @
- The privatisation of the Hungarian Electricity Works will be completed this year, said Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha.
NEPSZAVA

- Austrian Vice Chancellor and Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schussel on Thursday described bilateral ties as free from problems, as he looked forward to today's visit from Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs.
- A report on Hungary by the International Labour Organisation says one third of the country's population lives on or below the poverty line. @
NEPSZABADSAG

- Magda Kovacs Kosa, executive vice president of the Socialist Party has wound up a four-day visit to London, where she studied the methods of the political parties, particulary those of Labour in preparing for the upcoming general election.
- Agricultural producer prices between January and November of last year were 32.9 percent higher on average than in the same period of 1995.
VILAGGAZDASAG @

- Privatisation Minister Judit Csiha and Industry Minister Szabolcs Fazakas decided to maintain the existing privatisation strategy for the state oil and gas company MOL according to which there will be two share issues. The state will keep 25 percent plus one vote and a golden share.
- General Motors Europe will set up a new office in Budapest in early February to serve as the centre of GM's new regional organisation Opel Southeast Europe. @

- Analysts claim forint interest rates have achieved such a low level, that it will be no longer worthwhile to save in forints and speculation money may flow out of the country en masse unless the rate of the forint devaluation is reduced.
- The 2001/C five-year bond launched by Hungary yesterday was six times oversubscribed. The average yield was 15.09 percent on bonds worth a total HUF 5 billion.
- A total of 764,000 businesses were active at the end of December, 15 percent more than in the previous years.
-- Budapest newsroom (36 1) 327 4040
